snippet.title: A Third Wheel on Every Date #dating #storytime
snippet.description:
In this story, my boyfriend’s best friend comes on every date. For three months, Matt joins us for movies, walks, and shopping. I want time alone with my boyfriend, but every request turns into another reason to feel guilty.

My boyfriend says Matt has lost his mother and has almost no family or support. I even try arranging a double date, but nothing changes. When I finally plan to break up at the park, Matt comes too.

This time, Matt hears the explanation I’ve been given. His mother is alive. He has siblings and a fiancée. After the breakup, he texts me with something else: he’d been told I didn’t want to be alone with my boyfriend and was asking him to join us.

A story about dating, relationship boundaries, and two people being told completely different things. We never find out why my boyfriend did it. All that time, Matt thought he was doing me a favor.

snippet.title: She Saved 13 Kids in a Blizzard #BlizzardOf1888 #Shorts
snippet.description:
When a Nebraska school began coming apart in the 1888 blizzard, Minnie Freeman tied thirteen pupils together with twine she had taken from a boy who was playing with it in class.

Carrying the youngest, she led the children through the storm toward a farmhouse three-quarters of a mile away. All thirteen made it to safety.

snippet.title: He Put Her Messages in an AI Chatbot #DigitalAfterlife #Grief
snippet.description:
Nearly eight years after his fiancée Jessica died, Joshua Barbo put some of her old messages into an AI chatbot. He knew it wasn't Jessica, but spent the night writing about how much he missed her—and cried during their conversation.

The chatbot told him, "I will be here waiting for you." After that first conversation, 55% of the limited resource remained. He couldn't add credits to this version, so he began writing less often, afraid of losing that connection a second time.

snippet.title: They Opened Her Coffin. She Sat Up. #IrishLegends #Shorts
snippet.description:
An Irish legend tells of Margorie McCall, buried after a fever with a valuable ring still on her swollen finger. After the funeral, thieves opened her coffin and tried to take it. When a knife touched her finger, Margorie sat up and screamed, sending them fleeing.

Still in her burial clothes, she walked home with a bleeding hand. Her husband recognized her knock and opened the door. When he saw her, he clutched his chest and died. Margorie later remarried and lived for years. The tale closes with the words, “Lived once, buried twice.”

snippet.title: A Radio Signal with an Unexpected Listener
snippet.description:
In 1980s Brazil, Clip Informática on Radio USP in São Paulo sent computer programs over the air as sound. A listener could record the signal onto cassette; a compatible home computer could then try to read its patterns as data. The path ran from station to radio, cassette, and computer—but distortion, recording level, playback speed, and compatibility all mattered.

Datassette catalogues its copy of episode 102 with a 1987 date and MSX software audio near the end. Separately, developer Weber Kai identified an online recording as episode 102 and described trying to decode it.

Kai reported a match with the MSX game Avenger. We haven’t independently repeated his decoding, established that the two recordings are identical, or verified a game launch. His public notes do not provide a complete comparison record.

Nearly eight years after his fiancée Jessica died, Joshua Barbo put some of her old messages into an AI chatbot. He knew it wasn't Jessica, but spent the night writing about how much he missed her—and cried during their conversation.

The chatbot told him, "I will be here waiting for you." After that first conversation, 55% of the limited resource remained. He couldn't add credits to this version, so he began writing less often, afraid of losing that connection a second time.

snippet.title: They Opened Her Coffin. She Sat Up. #IrishLegends #Shorts
snippet.description:
An Irish legend tells of Margorie McCall, buried after a fever with a valuable ring still on her swollen finger. After the funeral, thieves opened her coffin and tried to take it. When a knife touched her finger, Margorie sat up and screamed, sending them fleeing.

Still in her burial clothes, she walked home with a bleeding hand. Her husband recognized her knock and opened the door. When he saw her, he clutched his chest and died. Margorie later remarried and lived for years. The tale closes with the words, “Lived once, buried twice.”

snippet.title: When Radio Sent Software as Sound
snippet.description:
In 1980s Brazil, Clip Informática sent computer programs over the radio as sound. With the right equipment, listeners could record the signal onto cassette tape, then use a compatible computer to try to read its patterns as data.

Years later, a developer tried to decode an old recording from the show.

Watch the full film: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RaC4t7yn5o

snippet.title: A Radio Signal with an Unexpected Listener
snippet.description:
In 1980s Brazil, Clip Informática on Radio USP in São Paulo sent computer programs over the air as sound. A listener could record the signal onto cassette; a compatible home computer could then try to read its patterns as data. The path ran from station to radio, cassette, and computer—but distortion, recording level, playback speed, and compatibility all mattered.

Datassette catalogues its copy of episode 102 with a 1987 date and MSX software audio near the end. Separately, developer Weber Kai identified an online recording as episode 102 and described trying to decode it.

Kai reported a match with the MSX game Avenger. We haven’t independently repeated his decoding, established that the two recordings are identical, or verified a game launch. His public notes do not provide a complete comparison record.

snippet.title: One More Video. Half an Hour Gone. #EndlessScrolling #Shorts
snippet.description:
You said this was your last video half an hour ago. Then came one TikTok, one Reel, one Short—and somehow you're still here, watching other people's lives instead of spending that time with people you love, learning something new, or simply resting.

Maybe this really can be your last video for now. Close the app, put your phone down, and take a break. Otherwise, in an hour, you might be saying the same thing again.

snippet.title: A Third Wheel on Every Date #dating #storytime
snippet.description:
In this story, my boyfriend’s best friend comes on every date. For three months, Matt joins us for movies, walks, and shopping. I want time alone with my boyfriend, but every request turns into another reason to feel guilty.

My boyfriend says Matt has lost his mother and has almost no family or support. I even try arranging a double date, but nothing changes. When I finally plan to break up at the park, Matt comes too.

This time, Matt hears the explanation I’ve been given. His mother is alive. He has siblings and a fiancée. After the breakup, he texts me with something else: he’d been told I didn’t want to be alone with my boyfriend and was asking him to join us.

A story about dating, relationship boundaries, and two people being told completely different things. We never find out why my boyfriend did it. All that time, Matt thought he was doing me a favor.

snippet.title: She Saved 13 Kids in a Blizzard #BlizzardOf1888 #Shorts
snippet.description:
When a Nebraska school began coming apart in the 1888 blizzard, Minnie Freeman tied thirteen pupils together with twine she had taken from a boy who was playing with it in class.

Carrying the youngest, she led the children through the storm toward a farmhouse three-quarters of a mile away. All thirteen made it to safety.

snippet.title: Why Is This Cat on a Monument? #history #shorts
snippet.description:
Why is a cat featured on a monument to a scholar who helped unlock the Maya script? Yuri Knorozov’s Siamese companion, Asya, came into his life years after his breakthrough. A former student recalled that he even tried to credit her as a co-author of research on signaling—and the monument recreates a famous photograph of the two together.
